definitions.explanation: The ability to sense or understand others' feelings, situations, or unspoken intentions without being told directly. A key concept in Japanese interpersonal communication.

examples.japanese: {察|さっ}しが{悪|わる}くて、{相手|あいて}の{気持|きも}ちに{気|き}づけなかった。
examples.english: I was insensitive and couldn't notice the other person's feelings.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}では{言葉|ことば}にしなくても{察|さっ}しで{通|つう}じることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: In Japan, things are often communicated through unspoken understanding rather than words.

notes:
{察|さっ}し is the noun form of {察|さっ}する (to sense, to perceive). It describes the ability to read between the lines and understand what is not explicitly stated.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {察|さっ}しがいい (perceptive, quick to pick up on things)
- {察|さっ}しが{悪|わる}い (insensitive, slow to pick up on things)
- {察|さっ}しがつく (to be able to guess/sense)
- お{察|さっ}しします (I can imagine how you feel — polite expression of empathy)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{察|さっ}し is considered a core aspect of Japanese communication style. Japanese culture places high value on being able to understand others' feelings and intentions without explicit verbal expression. Being described as {察|さっ}しがいい is a significant compliment, while {察|さっ}しが{悪|わる}い can be a pointed criticism.
